doc.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025

title: Digital recording and knowing when to stop
summary: In the digital era he tells producers that more tweaking is different, not better.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: And you’re in the digital world now.
Yeah. Is it harder to know when to stop? Because basically you can keep tweaking things to infinity.

Well I worked with some people that go past it. We get to the point where they should stop and they’re still looking to improve it so I developed the phrase, “Well what do you think? Is this better?” I would say, “It’s not better, it’s different.” So it got to a point where you didn’t make the record better, you just made it different. And the difference

was not enough to affect the feeling. So as a result of a lot of insecurities, people that I worked with that were producers wound up doing things and worked past where they should have stopped, where they had the record, they just went past it and lost it, lost the record.
